tours.name: The Reefs
tours.blurb: Limestone slabs stood on end where the Rockies override the plains — the cleanest mountain front in America.

keys.cap: Castle Reef, a single slab of Madison limestone shoved east over the prairie — the Front is a stack of such thrust sheets, laid like shingles.
Rocky Mountain, 9,392 ft — the highest point of the Front. Behind it the thrust sheets repeat westward, reef after reef, into the wilderness.
Ear Mountain, the landmark butte of the Teton country — a vision-quest site of the Blackfeet, and the mountain A.B. Guthrie wrote under.
Choteau Mountain and the long rampart north — every canyon a water gap sawed through the reefs at right angles.

tours.name: The Old North Trail
tours.blurb: A travois road older than memory runs along the mountain foot — the Blackfeet road from Canada to the south.

keys.cap: Heart Butte, under its namesake mountain — the oldest community on this part of the Blackfeet Nation, whose southern line the 1896 cession drew along Birch Creek.
The foothill bench the Old North Trail follows — travois ruts and tipi rings mark a road used for thousands of years, hugging the mountains where the water and shelter are.
Badger Creek and the old agency country. The Starvation Winter of 1883–84 happened here, in sight of these mountains, when the buffalo were gone and the annuities failed.
Morningstar and Feather Woman — the mountains carry Blackfeet star-story names; this wall is Miistákis, the Backbone of the World.

tours.name: Sun River
tours.blurb: The Sun cuts the whole Front in one gorge — medicine water to the Blackfeet, irrigation water to the valley below.

keys.cap: Sun River Canyon — the river the Blackfeet called Medicine saws straight through three reefs in a row.
The Gibson dam site. The 1903 Saypo sheet shows only the river; the dam came in 1929 — the modern terrain holds the reservoir the engraving never knew.
Out of the mountains toward Augusta, just off the sheet's south edge — stage road, wool town, and the diversion works that watered the bench.
Freezeout Lake on the flats — a stop on a flyway older than the trail itself; snow geese by the tens of thousands still stage here.

tours.name: The Teton
tours.blurb: Choteau's river — canyon, bench and butte country between the reefs and the wheat.

keys.cap: Choteau, seat of Teton County — named for the fur trader Pierre Chouteau; the town kept one 'u' and the county kept the pronunciation.
Pine Butte, the last outlier before the mountains — below it the swamp the grizzlies still walk out onto the plains to reach, the only place they do.
The Teton canyon under Ear Mountain — Guthrie's ranch sat here; 'The Big Sky' was written looking at this skyline.
Bynum on the bench — wool, wheat, and (though the 1920 sheet could not know it) the dinosaur beds in the Two Medicine rocks that would one day make the town famous.
